method: 390x844 portrait (aspect 0.46 < 0.74) forces the mobile render tier; raceAutoplay on both tracks; 18s/track, samples past raceTime>4s (governor warmup excluded); GL flags via scripts/lib/chromium-gl-args.mjs.
caveat: Absolute fps is THIS machine's GPU, not a phone's. Portable signals are frameWorkMs (CPU work), drawCalls/gpuCalls (submission cost) and renderScale/postChainEnabled (mobile tier active). Real phone GPU frame time is not measurable here — the adaptive governor self-protects against it.
interpretation: CPU frame work is ~11-12% of the 60fps budget on both tracks — the CPU is NOT a bottleneck at the mobile tier, so post-chain tiering (which trims GPU work) would not help the number that is portable to a phone.

The post chain is ALREADY aggressively mobile-tiered (architecture map): MSAA off, SMAA off, bloomTight lobe dropped, bloom mip levels 4 (vs 6), LUT tetrahedral interp off, grain/aerial-haze/speed-blur reduced. The owner-approved grades survive: ACES tone map + per-track LUT3D + vignette stay on every tier.

The governor climbs render scale to near-ceiling on this machine (headroom), and self-limits on slower GPUs — so the mobile tier is self-protecting against phone GPU cost that cannot be measured on this desktop.

The one PORTABLE mobile-GPU lever measured: Penguin Village submits 218 gpuCalls vs Comeback City's 71 (3x). Draw-call count is a real per-frame submission cost on mobile. That is a draw-call-reduction task (instancing/merging), verifiable via gpuCalls before/after — folded into item 8, NOT post-chain trimming.

decision.6c-post-chain-tiering: NO speculative change. No measured CPU deficit; the chain is already binary-tiered for mobile; further GPU tiering is unverifiable without a real phone (would be a wave-6-class unverified render change, violating standing rules 5 and 12). Closed as 'already tiered — no measured further work'.
decision.next: item 7 (elevation) — a clear, measurable, high-value lever. PV draw-call reduction added to item 8.
